speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatic Hydrothorax secondary to Congenital Biliary Atresia. The clinical picture of rapid breathing (likely due to hydrothorax from liver disease), pitting edema, hepatomegaly, and a normal BNP in a child with an incidental ASD strongly points to severe liver failure rather than primary cardiac failure. The ASD is likely an incidental finding or a result of chronic hypoxia from the lung effusion.
